title: Geography Construction
source: WWN Deluxe — Creating Your Campaign · Geography Construction (pp.124-127) & Placing Ruins and Points of Interest (p.150)

entries.value: Ancient farmland — a huge stretch of land re-engineered for optimal farming
Arratu wasteland — once xenoformed by the Outsiders into an environment hostile to humanity, or inhabited by dangerous alien lifeforms
Blasted lands — radioactive or scorched over by ancient war; many ruins are likely
Canyons — extensive canyons cut by rivers present or long-vanished (rivers don't climb after leaving them)
Dense forest — trackless, dark, and an effective natural barrier
Grasslands — a broad sweep of savanna or grassy plains as a coherent whole
Islands — a single significant island off the coast or an archipelago of note
Jagged mountains — a young, tall mountain range forming a barrier; likely casts a substantial rain shadow
Jungle — a classic adventure-worthy jungle of wild, semi-alien flora and fauna
Light forest — interspersed with other terrain
Megaplex — the ruins of a single huge ancient structure stretching for endless miles
Pit — a Deep or other underground megastructure collapsed, leaving a hole tens of miles across
Rain forest — vast, damp, and green
Rocky hills — rough and stony, little arable land; herding and raiding most profitable
Rolling hills — gently rolling hills make for good agricultural land
Sand desert — a waste of sand and dunes, from rain shadow or legacy of ancient war
Scrub desert — often on the leeward side of mountain ranges; borders are often grassland or savanna
Swamp — a sinking river, lake margin, or wet coastal delta forms a vast bog in flat land
Volcano — one or more mountains nearby are volcanically active, naturally or by Legacy flux
Weathered mountains — rounded, low mountains with a skirt of hills; limited rain shadow
